title: Spell Formula 1: The for Loop
lessonSummary: Well done! The for loop repeats code – and range(n) counts from 0 for you.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the output below.
tasks.codeTemplate:
print("The Tower of Repetitions opens!")
for i in range(5):
    print(f"Run {i}: The value of i is {i}")
print("Done!")

validation.expected: Run 4: The value of i is 4

tasks.instruction: Use a for loop with range(3) to print these three lines: Spell 0, Spell 1 and Spell 2 (each on its own line).
Create count = 0, let the loop run 4 times and increase count by 1 each time. Afterwards print exactly: Finished casting: 4 times

title: Spell Formula 1: range() with start and end
lessonSummary: You can now start counting at any number – but the end never counts!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the 8 is no longer counted!
tasks.codeTemplate:
print("=== Counting from 3 to 7 ===")
for number in range(3, 8):
    print(f"Number: {number}")
print("The 8 is not included!")

tasks.instruction: Print the numbers from 10 to 14, each in the form Number: 10, Number: 11 and so on (up to Number: 14).
You climb the tower: print floors 1 to 6, each as Floor 1, Floor 2 … up to Floor 6.

title: Spell Formula 1: Step size and counting backwards
lessonSummary: With a third number you jump in steps – and with a negative step you count backwards.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: first up in steps of two, then backwards.
Count in steps of five from 5 to 25 and print each number as Step: 5, Step: 10 … up to Step: 25.
Start a countdown: count backwards from 5 to 1 and print each number in the form 5..., 4... and so on (down to 1...). Afterwards print Launch!

title: Spell Formula 1: Looping through letters
lessonSummary: You can loop through texts too – letter by letter.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the loop goes through the text letter by letter.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Aria"
print(f"The name is: {name}")
for letter in name:
    print(f"  - {letter}")
print("Done!")

tasks.instruction: Go through the text "Dragon" with a for loop and print each letter in the form - D, - r, - a … .
Use a for loop to count the letters of spell (variable count, start 0) and print exactly: Letters: 11

title: Spell Formula 2: The while Loop
lessonSummary: The Guardian of the Condition: while repeats as long as the condition is true.

tasks.instruction: Run this example.
tasks.codeTemplate:
counter = 0
while counter <= 5:
    print(f"Counter: {counter}")
    counter += 1  # IMPORTANT: otherwise an endless loop!
print("At 6 the condition becomes false – stop!")

tasks.instruction: Count from 1 to 4 with a while loop and print each number as Round 1, Round 2 … up to Round 4.
As long as gold is smaller than 100, double it (gold = gold * 2). Afterwards print exactly: Gold: 128

title: Spell Formula 2: The game loop
lessonSummary: This is exactly how games work: they run until the health is used up.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the hero loses 20 health every round.
tasks.codeTemplate:
health = 100
round_number = 1

while health > 0:
    damage = 20
    health -= damage
    print(f"Round {round_number}: -{damage} health, left: {health}")
    round_number += 1

print(f"Game over after {round_number - 1} rounds!")

tasks.instruction: A hero has 50 health and loses 10 per round. Let the loop run until health is no longer greater than 0, and count the rounds. Afterwards print exactly: Hero fallen after 5 rounds
A wizard has 30 mana, every spell costs 8. Cast spells as long as mana is at least 8 (count them in spell_count). Afterwards print exactly: Spells cast: 3, mana left: 6

title: Spell Formula 3: Nested loops
lessonSummary: The Double Spiral: the inner loop runs through completely on every run of the outer one.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: three towers with two floors each.
Use two nested loops to print all rooms: the outer loop counts corridors from 1 to 2, the inner loop doors from 1 to 3. Each line has the form Room 1-1, Room 1-2 … up to Room 2-3.
With nested loops (outer range(4), inner range(5)) count in the variable count how often the inner loop runs in total. Afterwards print exactly: Total: 20

title: Spell Formula 3: Patterns of stars
lessonSummary: With nested loops you draw whole patterns – row by row.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a rectangle made of stars.
Draw 3 rows with exactly 5 stars * each (no spaces in between, so *****). Use print("*", end="") in the inner loop and an empty print() after every row.
Draw a staircase of stars: row 1 has one *, row 2 has two ** and so on up to row 4 with ****. Tip: range(1, 5) for the rows and range(row) for the columns.

title: Mission 2: The Guardian of the Tower
lessonSummary: You checked all ten floors – with for and while!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Climbing the tower: Go through all floors from 1 to 10 and print for each: Floor 1: All quiet... (up to Floor 10: All quiet...).
Step 2 – Warnings: On floors 3, 6 and 9 print a warning in the form Magical disturbance on floor 3. Tip: range(3, 10, 3).
Step 3 – Maintenance: Go through all floors from 1 to 10. On floor 7 (compare with ==) print only Floor 7 is closed for repairs, on all others Floor N: All quiet...
Step 4 – Conquer the tower: Use a while loop to climb up from floor 1 as long as floor is smaller than 10 (increase it by 1 each time). Afterwards print exactly: Tower conquered: Floor 10

title: Mission 3: The Endless Labyrinth
lessonSummary: You found the exit – with cleverly chosen conditions!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Find the exit: You are at position = 0 and steps = 0. Use a while loop, as long as position is smaller than 20, to move 2 positions further with every step (increase steps by 1). Afterwards print exactly: Exit reached after 10 steps
Step 2 – Status messages: Every 10 steps from 10 to 100 print a message (the position is twice the step), e.g. Step 10: Position 20 and finally Step 100: Position 200. Tip: range(10, 101, 10).

Step 3 – Lost?: You move 3 positions per step, the exit is at 50. Use a while loop, as long as position is smaller than 50 and steps is smaller than 10. If you are still below 50 afterwards, print exactly: Lost in the labyrinth after 10 steps

validation.expected: Lost in the labyrinth after 10 steps
